prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows a flat ground plane sloping away from the camera wearer across an open nighttime sports field, with goal frames, a small building, and light poles located roughly 10 to 25 metres in the background of frames 1 and 2 before panning left across the field in frames 3 to 5. In frame 1, two people stand at about 6 to 8 metres ahead (center-left in teal facing the wearer, and far right partially cut off by the frame edge, roughly 5 metres apart), while in frame 2 two people in black are at about 4 metres (left, facing away) and 6 metres (right, facing the wearer) and separated by roughly 3 metres. During rapid camera turning in frames 3 and 4, a nearby person at 2 to 3 metres on the bottom-left and two more distant people at 5 to 10 metres appear as faint, blurry depth blobs, whereas frame 5 clearly resolves a person on the far right at 2 to 3 metres facing away alongside two people on the left at roughly 7 to 8 metres who are within about 1 metre of each other (nearly within each other's arm's reach, though nothing is within arm's reach of the camera wearer in any frame). Compared to the dark RGB strip, the depth map makes the continuous ground surface, background goal frame, building, and tall light pole in frame 1 much easier to distinguish from the dark sky. However, the depth map is unreliable during heavy motion blur in frames 3 and 4 where player silhouettes nearly vanish into the ground gradient, and it truncates the heads of the people in frame 2.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates subsets of the players on the field against a black background across the five frames, showing how the camera wearer pans right in frame 2 and then sweeps left from frame 3 to frame 5. In frame 1 it segments the person at 6 metres center-left (facing the wearer, with an overlapping duplicate label for a distant background figure right behind them) and the partially cropped person at 7 metres on the right edge, while in frame 2 it captures the closer person at 4 metres on the left (facing away) and the person at 6 metres on the right (facing the wearer, split into overlapping torso and leg masks). Across frames 3 and 4, as the camera turns rapidly left, the segmentation map completely misses the blurred people in the foreground and midground at 2 to 10 metres, before re-detecting the two people on the left at 7 to 8 metres (who stand within arm's reach of each other, one facing right and one facing left) and the close person at 2 to 3 metres on the bottom-right (facing away, legs partially cropped by the lower frame border) in frame 5. While the masks help confirm the boundaries of the dimly lit pair on the left in frame 5 and the tiny occluded person directly behind the teal player in frame 1 that are hard to separate in RGB, nothing is within arm's reach of the camera wearer. The map is highly unreliable under motion blur and low light, failing to detect any players in frames 3 and 4, hallucinating 'airplane' labels on streaked stadium floodlights in the upper sky of frames 3 and 4, and fragmenting single bodies into multiple masks in frames 2 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map detects only two people across the entire five-frame sequence—one in frame 1, one in frame 2, and one in frame 5—while leaving the rest of the field and all other individuals blank. In frame 1, a yellow body skeleton at the bottom-left marks the person about 6 metres away leaning left with their torso angled toward the camera wearer and right arm extended to their side, but misses their left leg. In frame 2, a single skeleton about 4 metres away on the left shows the shoulder, hip, and leg joints of a person facing away from the camera wearer and moving forward into the field as the viewpoint pans right. After detecting no skeletons at all during the rapid leftward head turn in frames 3 and 4, the map captures the close person on the bottom-right of frame 5 at 2 to 3 metres away facing away and running forward with their lower legs extending past the bottom edge of the frame. Although the skeleton joints make the limb articulation and forward-leaning posture of the close runners in frames 1, 2, and 5 clearer than in the dark RGB images, the pose map is very unreliable for full-scene spatial understanding because it misses all distant and motion-blurred people (including the pair within arm's reach of each other in frame 5) and detects no magenta hand skeletons in any frame.
